transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Less than three weeks before the midterm elections, President Trump is concentrating primarily
on red states.
Today, he has stops in Arizona and Montana, and Pierre Stephen Fowler says next week the
president heads to Kansas, which has become a newly competitive state.
Kansas is a state with an outgoing Democratic governor and a Republican U.S. Senator on
the ballot, but polls show voters could pick a Republican to retake the governor's office
and send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century.
On the one hand, the president's deeply unpopular economic policies have hit states like Kansas
hard.
On the other, Republicans have been appealing to voters with local solutions to issues like
affordability and lower energy prices in their bid for the governor's seat, which leads to
Trump spending one of the final days of the midterms in Wichita, campaigning in a state
he won by more than 16 points in 2024.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Dodge City, Kansas.
With the economy on the minds of many voters, consumer prices rose 3.7 percent in September
from a year ago, according to a report today from the Labor Department.
It was up from 3.4 percent in August and a little higher than forecasts for a 3.6 percent
increase.
While measured monthly, the consumer price index rose 6.10 percent last month from August.
The faculty senate at Cornell University is meeting today.
Members are beginning the process of voting no confidence in university leadership in response
to the school's handling of an alleged gang rape on campus in 2024.
And here's a listen.
Ed Wernie has more.
The university announced changes to campus policies, including banning fraternity parties
through the end of the year, but faculty still intend to use today's meeting to begin the
process of voting no confidence.
Anne Marie Brady is a member of the faculty senate who co-signed the motion.
There's a great sense of anger and I think also sadness.
We have lost confidence in the administration to effectively address sexual assault and
sexual harassment on campus.
Over the weekend, more than 200 faculty and staff signed a letter to students that said,
"This administration does not speak for us."
They say the university has failed to keep students safe and more change is needed.
Alison Adwornie, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
Anthropic warns we may be just months away from artificial intelligent bots that can
self-replicate and take over internet connected devices.
More from NPR's John Ruich.
Anthropic says some large AI models can already self-replicate and it predicts that smaller
ones could catch up by the end of the year.
That could lead to so-called AI worms that get into online systems like smart TVs or other
internet enabled devices and replicate.
Data centers could also be a target, since there's no central on/off switch for bots
like this, they could be hard to stop.
Anthropic says they could spread like "digital slime mold" expanding in a matter of days.
The warning in a blog post could add to concerns about control over AI as its capabilities
grow.
It's NPR.
Netflix could be eliminating nearly a thousand jobs, the Associated Press reports.
It obtained a memo set out by the co-CEO's of the streaming powerhouse informing employees
of company plans to reduce Netflix's workforce by about 6 percent.
They state in that memo the biggest cuts will be in the areas of tech, legal, product and
human resources.
Netflix's profit grew this year, however its third quarter earnings to be released next
week are projected to fall below Wall Street's expectations as it faces more streaming competition.
Ahead of the midterm vote, a new survey shows white evangelicals are the lone group of registered
voters in the United States in which a majority favor Republican candidates running for a
seat in the House.
NPR's Jason DeRose reports on the findings from Pew Research.
Nearly three-quarters of white evangelical Protestants expect to vote for their congressional
district's Republican candidate.
Pew Research also found white Catholic voters favor Republicans, though by a much narrower
margin.
Those more likely to support Democrats include black Protestants, Hispanic Catholics, atheists,
agnostics, and those who describe their religion as nothing in particular.
Regarding President Trump, white evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in
which a majority now approves of his job performance.
However, Pew found that approval has dropped by 20 points since his return to office.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
U.S. stocks trading lower at the Dow now down 175 points.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump concentrates midterm campaigning on red states, including a Wichita, Kansas stop
Consumer prices rise 3.7 percent in September from a year earlier, Labor Department reports
Cornell faculty senate begins process of voting no confidence in leadership over 2024 gang rape case
Anthropic warns AI models may soon self-replicate and spread across internet-connected devices
Netflix plans to cut about 6 percent of its workforce, nearly a thousand jobs, per AP
Pew survey finds white evangelical voters favor Republican House candidates, Trump approval drops 20 points
